name: Butter
melt_note: Yes — this conversion is for solid butter measured by packing into the cup. Melted butter is measured the same way by volume, but if a recipe calls for 'melted then measured,' pack it solid first for accuracy since melting can trap air pockets that skew volume.

name: Coconut Oil
melt_note: Yes — coconut oil is solid below about 76°F (24°C) and liquid above it. Measure solid coconut oil by packing it into the cup like butter; measured liquid coconut oil will weigh very slightly less per cup due to lower density in its melted state.

name: Margarine
melt_note: Margarine has a very similar density to butter, so the solid-vs-melted consideration is the same: pack solid margarine into the cup for the most accurate measurement.

name: Vegetable Shortening
melt_note: Shortening is always solid at room temperature and should be packed into the measuring cup, pressing out air pockets, for an accurate weight.

name: Vegetable Oil
melt_note: Vegetable oil is liquid at room temperature, so there's no solid-vs-melted distinction — just measure directly with a liquid measuring cup for best accuracy.

name: Olive Oil
melt_note: Olive oil is liquid at room temperature. Use a liquid measuring cup rather than a dry one for the most accurate volume reading.

name: Granulated Sugar
melt_note: Granulated sugar doesn't melt for measurement purposes — this conversion assumes standard dry granulated sugar spooned into the cup and leveled off.

name: Brown Sugar
melt_note: This conversion assumes firmly packed brown sugar, which is the standard most recipes intend. Loosely measured brown sugar can weigh 15–20% less per cup.

name: Powdered Sugar
melt_note: Powdered sugar should be spooned lightly into the cup and leveled, not packed or sifted directly in the cup, for the most consistent measurement.

name: Honey
melt_note: Honey is measured as a liquid regardless of temperature, though slightly warming it makes it easier to pour cleanly and level in the measuring cup.

name: Maple Syrup
melt_note: Maple syrup is measured as a liquid at any normal serving temperature; no solid state applies.

name: All-Purpose Flour
melt_note: Flour doesn't melt, but measurement technique matters a lot here: spoon flour into the cup and level it off rather than scooping directly with the cup, which can compact it and add up to 20% extra weight.

name: Whole Wheat Flour
melt_note: As with all-purpose flour, spoon-and-level is the accurate technique — scooping directly compacts the flour and skews the weight higher.

name: Almond Flour
melt_note: Almond flour is lighter and more prone to clumping than wheat flour — spoon it in and level gently rather than pressing it down.

name: Cornstarch
melt_note: Cornstarch should be spooned and leveled like flour; it settles and compacts easily if scooped straight from the container.

name: Cocoa Powder
melt_note: Cocoa powder clumps easily — sift before measuring for the most accurate and consistent result.

name: Rolled Oats
melt_note: Oats are measured dry and don't compact meaningfully, so a level scoop straight from the container is accurate.

name: White Rice
melt_note: Uncooked rice doesn't compact significantly, so scooping and leveling gives a reliably accurate measurement.

name: Quinoa
melt_note: Uncooked quinoa measures consistently whether scooped or spooned, since the small grains settle evenly.

name: Breadcrumbs
melt_note: Dry breadcrumbs should be spooned lightly into the cup; packing them down can add meaningfully to the weight.

name: Table Salt
melt_note: This conversion is for fine table salt. Coarser salts like kosher or sea salt are less dense by volume and will weigh noticeably less per cup.

name: Milk
melt_note: Milk is measured as a liquid at any standard temperature; use a liquid measuring cup for the most accurate reading.

name: Heavy Cream
melt_note: Heavy cream is measured as a liquid; no solid-vs-melted consideration applies.

name: Water
melt_note: Water is the reference liquid for volume-to-weight conversion — 1 cup is defined as almost exactly 237g at room temperature.

name: Baking Powder
melt_note: Baking powder should be measured level, straight from the container, without packing — excess pressure can affect how it reacts when baked.

name: Baking Soda
melt_note: Baking soda is fine and dense — spoon it in and level with a knife edge rather than shaking the cup to settle it, which can pack it too tightly.

name: Ground Cinnamon
melt_note: Ground cinnamon doesn't melt — this conversion assumes it's spooned into the cup and leveled, not packed, since packing spices can add 10-15% extra weight.

name: Ground Nutmeg
melt_note: Freshly ground nutmeg is finer and slightly denser than pre-ground jarred nutmeg — this conversion uses standard pre-ground nutmeg as the baseline.

name: Ground Ginger
melt_note: Ground ginger settles over time in storage — give the jar a shake before spooning to loosen it for a more accurate scoop.

name: Paprika
melt_note: Smoked and sweet paprika have essentially the same density — this conversion applies to both.

name: Ground Black Pepper
melt_note: Freshly cracked pepper is coarser and less dense than pre-ground — this conversion assumes standard fine-ground black pepper.

name: Chili Powder
melt_note: Chili powder blends vary slightly by brand depending on filler ingredients, but this conversion holds for standard commercial chili powder.

name: Ground Cumin
melt_note: Ground cumin should be spooned and leveled rather than scooped directly, since scooping can compact it and skew the weight slightly higher.

name: Sliced Almonds
melt_note: This conversion is for sliced almonds; whole or chopped almonds pack differently and will weigh a different amount per cup.

name: Chopped Walnuts
melt_note: Coarsely chopped walnuts pack more loosely than finely chopped — this conversion assumes a medium, roughly-chopped texture.

name: Chopped Pecans
melt_note: As with other chopped nuts, chop size affects packing density — this conversion assumes a medium chop.

name: Chopped Peanuts
melt_note: Peanuts are denser than most tree nuts, so they weigh more per cup even at a similar chop size.

name: Cashews
melt_note: This conversion is for whole raw cashews; roughly chopped cashews will pack slightly differently.

name: Shredded Coconut
melt_note: Unsweetened shredded coconut is lighter than sweetened, flaked versions — this conversion is for standard unsweetened shredded coconut.

name: Sour Cream
melt_note: Sour cream is measured cold, straight from the container — there's no melted state to account for.

name: Plain Yogurt
melt_note: Greek yogurt is thicker and denser than regular yogurt and will weigh somewhat more per cup — this conversion is for standard plain yogurt.

name: Cream Cheese
melt_note: This conversion is for cream cheese at room temperature, packed into the cup. Cold, firm cream cheese is harder to measure accurately by volume.

name: Grated Parmesan
melt_note: This conversion is for finely grated Parmesan, lightly spooned into the cup. Pre-shredded, coarser Parmesan will weigh less per cup.

name: Shredded Cheddar
melt_note: Shredded cheese should be measured loosely packed, not pressed down, for the most standard and accurate result.

name: Ricotta Cheese
melt_note: Ricotta is measured cold, spooned into the cup — there's no melted state to account for in this conversion.

name: Chopped Onion
melt_note: This conversion is for raw, medium-diced onion, loosely packed into the cup.

name: Diced Tomato
melt_note: This conversion is for fresh diced tomato without excess liquid drained off; canned diced tomato with juice will weigh slightly more.

name: Mashed Banana
melt_note: This conversion is for ripe mashed banana, spooned into the cup without pressing air pockets out.

name: Grated Carrot
melt_note: This conversion is for finely grated raw carrot, loosely packed into the cup.

name: Chopped Celery
melt_note: This conversion is for raw, medium-diced celery, loosely packed into the cup.

name: Corn Syrup
melt_note: Corn syrup is measured as a liquid at room temperature; there's no solid state to account for.

name: Molasses
melt_note: Molasses is measured as a liquid. Lightly greasing the measuring cup first can help it pour out cleanly without affecting the measurement.

name: White Vinegar
melt_note: White vinegar is measured as a liquid at any standard temperature; no solid state applies.

name: Erythritol
melt_note: Erythritol is a dry granular sweetener and doesn't melt for measurement purposes — spoon and level for accuracy, since it's lighter than table sugar by volume.

name: Cornmeal
melt_note: Cornmeal doesn't compact significantly, so a level scoop straight from the container is accurate.

name: Semolina
melt_note: Semolina is coarser than flour and doesn't compact the same way — a level scoop is accurate without needing to spoon and level.

name: Dried Lentils
melt_note: Dried lentils measure consistently by volume since the small, uniform pieces settle evenly.

name: Dried Chickpeas
melt_note: Dried chickpeas measure consistently whether scooped or spooned, since the rounded shape settles evenly in the cup.

name: Panko Breadcrumbs
melt_note: Panko is much lighter and airier than standard breadcrumbs — don't pack it into the cup, or the weight will read significantly higher than actual.
